title: Reward Valuation in Large Language Models: Causal Induction of Anhedonia
abstract: arXiv:2607.06626v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Recent frontier models mimic complex aspects of human cognition. Here we ask whether this alignment extends into reward valuation, which we assess in a mechanistic framework. Specifically, we use clinical tests that were developed to evaluate anhedonia in human subjects with major depressive disorders. Mechanistically, anhedonia is frequently associated with dysregulation in the Nucleus Accumbens (NAc) and the broader dopaminergic reward system. While neuroimaging has localized these deficits, establishing a causal link between NAc activity and specific behavioral symptoms remains a challenge. We use these ideas from neuroscience to functionally identify reward-anticipatory units in state-of-the-art AI models, and evaluate their causal involvement via targeted perturbations. We find that not only are such model units predictive of NAc brain recordings, their perturbation also induces behavioral effects mirroring human anhedonia: the

translated_title: 大型语言模型中的奖励估值：快感缺失的因果诱导
translated_abstract: 近期最前沿的模型能够模拟人类认知的复杂方面。在此我们探讨这种对齐是否延伸到奖励估值领域，并在机制框架下对其进行评估。具体而言，我们使用了为评估重度抑郁症患者快感缺失而开发的临床测试。在机制层面上，快感缺失通常与伏隔核（NAc）及更广泛的多巴胺能奖励系统的功能失调相关。尽管神经影像学已对这些缺陷进行了定位，但在伏隔核活动与特定行为症状之间建立因果联系仍然是一个挑战。我们借助这些神经科学思想，在最新的AI模型中从功能上识别出预期奖励的单元，并通过有针对性的扰动评估其因果作用。我们发现，这些模型单元不仅能预测伏隔核的脑部记录，而且对其扰动还能诱导出与人类快感缺失相似的行为效应。
tldr: 该研究借鉴神经科学方法，在大语言模型中识别出能预测伏隔核脑信号的奖励预期单元，并通过定向扰动这些单元，在模型中成功诱导出类似人类快感缺失的行为效应，从而建立了奖励机制的因果联系。
en_tdlr: Borrowing from neuroscience, this study identifies reward-anticipatory units in large language models that predict Nucleus Accumbens recordings and demonstrates that targeted perturbation of these units causally induces anhedonia-like behavioral effects.
